---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 3: compile the Bayesian models"
---

Step 3 of the paper simulation (ML design): compile the brms models once (cmdstanr, no sampling). The
fitting step refits these templates on every dataset with `update(recompile = FALSE)`.

**Models**

| Model | Recall part | Precision / FP part | Slide effects |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Binomial + Poisson (main model) | TP ~ Bin(P, recall) | FP ~ Poisson | independent |
| Multinomial (comparison model) | (TP, FN, FP) ~ Multinomial(N), reference TP | muFP with P_log | independent |

- P_log = log(P) centred on the mean of log(P) of the dataset.
- brms default priors, except the intercept of the FP part in the binomial + Poisson model:
  student_t(3, 1, 2.5) on log FP. The brms default is centred on the log median FP count of the
  data, so it would depend on the compile data.

**Compile data:** scenario C, 40 slides, rep 1, variant 1. Any dataset works: Stan does not fix the
data dimensions at compile time, so one template fits 40 and 100 slides and all scenarios.

**Output** (`simulation/models/`)

- The executables of the models.
- `03_brms_templates.rds`: named list of the compiled templates.
- `03_model_versions.csv`: R, brms, cmdstanr and CmdStan versions and the compile data.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
library(brms)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# Columns for the binomial + Poisson model (GroundTruth = P trials of the recall part) and the
# multinomial model (Y, N, P_log)
prepare_brms_data <- function(df_sim) {
  df_sim |>
    mutate(
      # Binomial + Poisson
      GroundTruth = TP + FN,    # Sensitivity/recall trials: all true objects (P)
      # Multinomial
      N = TP + FN + FP,         # trials: all counted cells
      Y = cbind(TP = TP, FN = FN, FP = FP),
      # Object density, centred on the mean of log(P)
      P_log = as.numeric(scale(log(P), center = TRUE, scale = FALSE))
    )
}
```

# Load data
```{r}
df_counts <- read_csv("simulation/data/02_ML_performance_observed_data.csv.xz")

df_compile <- df_counts |>
  filter(scenario == "C", n_slide == 40, rep == 1, variant == 1) |>
  prepare_brms_data()
```

# Models
```{r}
# Binomial + Poisson: TP ~ Bin(P, recall), FP ~ Poisson(mu) independent of TP,
# independent slide effects for logit recall and log FP (no shared label)
bf_pois_tp <- bf(TP | trials(GroundTruth) ~ 1 + (1|slide), family = binomial())
bf_pois_fp <- bf(FP ~ 1 + (1|slide), family = poisson())

# Multinomial over (TP, FN, FP) with TP as reference category: muFN = -logit(recall),
# muFP = -logit(precision) with P_log; independent slide effects (no shared label)
bf_mult <- bf(Y | trials(N) ~ 1,
              muFN ~ 1 + (1|slide),
              muFP ~ 1 + P_log + (1|slide),
              family = multinomial(refcat = "TP"))

model_formulas <- list(
  "Binomial + Poisson" = bf_pois_tp + bf_pois_fp,
  "Multinomial"        = bf_mult
)

# Fixed intercept prior of the FP part (the brms default depends on the data);
# all other priors are brms defaults
model_priors <- list(
  "Binomial + Poisson" = prior(student_t(3, 1, 2.5), class = Intercept, resp = FP)
)
```

# Compile
```{r}
dir_models <- "simulation/models"
dir.create(dir_models, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Compile once without sampling (chains = 0). The executables go into dir_models
# (absolute path, so they are found from any working directory).
brms_templates <- imap(model_formulas, \(formula, model)
  brm(formula, data = df_compile, prior = model_priors[[model]],
      backend = "cmdstanr", chains = 0, refresh = 0,
      stan_model_args = list(dir = normalizePath(dir_models)))
)
```

# Save
```{r}
saveRDS(brms_templates, file.path(dir_models, "03_brms_templates.rds"))

tibble(
  r_version        = R.version.string,
  brms             = as.character(packageVersion("brms")),
  cmdstanr         = as.character(packageVersion("cmdstanr")),
  cmdstan          = cmdstanr::cmdstan_version(),
  compile_scenario = "C",
  compile_n_slide  = 40,
  compile_rep      = 1,
  compile_variant  = 1,
  created          = format(Sys.time())
) |>
  write_csv(file.path(dir_models, "03_model_versions.csv"))
```

# Check: default priors of another dataset
```{r}
# brms writes the priors into the Stan code, and some default priors depend on the data.
# update(recompile = FALSE) reuses the compiled executable, so every fit uses the priors of the
# template. Compare for very different datasets (scenario A variant 4, scenario D variant 1):
# expected difference: only the fixed FP intercept prior.
list(A = c("A", 4), D = c("D", 1)) |>
  map(\(x) {
    df_check <- df_counts |>
      filter(scenario == x[1], n_slide == 40, rep == 1, variant == as.numeric(x[2])) |>
      prepare_brms_data()
    imap(brms_templates, \(template, model) {
      list(template = prior_summary(template),
           default  = default_prior(formula(template), data = df_check)) |>
        map(\(priors) as_tibble(priors) |> select(prior, class, coef, group, resp, dpar)) |>
        bind_rows(.id = "source_prior") |>
        mutate(model = model)
    }) |>
      bind_rows() |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = source_prior, values_from = prior) |>
      filter(template != default) |>
      select(model, class, resp, dpar, group, template, default)
  })
```
